title: JSON key / sort field spliced into a SQL identifier position (ORDER BY, column)
index_line: T-0002 · SQL_EXEC · identifier-position injection via keys · blind error-iteration loop · corroborated
invariant_violated: The app treats a JSON key or sort parameter as a data label; the SQL layer splices it into an identifier position that parameter binding cannot express.

mechanism.does: attacker controls a KEY, not a value: sort/order_by/filter[<name>]/columns[]
server maps the key to a SQL identifier
identifier spliced unbound — binding an identifier is impossible in every dialect
DB parser error on unbalanced key becomes the oracle: break, fingerprint dialect, balance, refine
impact via CASE-in-ORDER-BY boolean flip or error-based extraction

source.http.body.value: JSON keys: sort, sort_by, orderBy, order, column, field, group_by, columns[], filter[<key>]

sink.sql.concat.value: identifier position (ORDER BY / dynamic WHERE / projection)

encoding.string.value: trailing quote to break, then balanced close with dialect comment (name'-- -)

oracle.error.value: Unknown column / unterminated quoted string / Incorrect syntax near — the DB parser names your key

guard.none.value: keys are almost never allowlisted the way values are

preconditions.expr: request keys reach the query builder
varies — sort/filter params usually need standard user auth only

success: DB error on key with trailing quote, absent on the clean key
balanced close parses clean while bare quote errored — the differential
CASE-based ORDER BY flips row order on a true/false condition
failure_like: keys allowlisted server-side — trailing quote yields no DB error
no error at all: parameter is bound as a value elsewhere
false_positive: error comes from the JSON parser, not the DB parser
value-oriented scanner noise on the same endpoint (values bound separately — that surface is T-0001)

hazards: error-message dialects differ (MySQL vs pg vs MSSQL vs SQLite wording) — fingerprint before balancing
value-oriented DAST misses this surface entirely
non_transfers: endpoints where sort fields are hardcoded enums
drivers that force-bind identifiers (rare; usually a builder DSL)
